reserved.$comment: Display names reserved for CNPJ-verified accounts (security.md rule 8). Compared after normalisation (lowercase, diacritics stripped, homoglyphs folded). Starter list: review before launch. The match is exact, so a name inside a longer display name ('bpc' in a personal name) does not collide; a common suffix such as 'oficial' needs its own entry. Federal programme names (bipe-chat/bipe#655, 30 October 2026) are in government.

family.$comment: Relationship terms that trigger the mismatch check when a chat uses them and the verified name does not match the contact (security.md rule 3). Compared after normalisation. Starter list: review before launch.

scam.$comment: On-device money-request detection (security.md rule 9). Friction, not protection: attackers can read these rules. Regexes use a portable ASCII subset: [0-9] not \\d, explicit (?<![0-9A-Za-z]) / (?![0-9A-Za-z]) instead of \\b, because ICU (Swift) and Java treat \\d and \\b as Unicode-aware while JS does not. Phrases are compared after normalisation. Starter list: review before launch. Warning kind: the first kind in warningKindPriority whose rule applies. pixKey applies only when the normalised message also contains a pixKeyContextWords entry (a phone number or e-mail alone is normal chat). newNumber applies when a matched urgency phrase is in newNumberPhrases (the falso parente opener), or when the normalised message contains a newAccountPhrases entry and also a registries/family-terms.json term as a whole word or a matched urgency phrase. On Bipe nobody sees phone numbers (ADR 0015), so the opener says new account instead of new number. Whole word: replace each run of characters outside [0-9a-z] in the normalised message with one space, then look for the term with a space on each side. newAccountPhrases need the context because "conta nova" alone is normal chat (a bank account, a new account on another app). Link hosts: linkPatterns matches (every match) on the host-folded message, which is normalize(message) with registries/homoglyphs.json except its ASCII keys outside [0-9a-z] (@, $ and | cannot be part of a host name). Each folded host has a plain host: the same UTF-16 range in normalize(message) without folding. deliveryFee (the fake-delivery fee scam: parcel held, pay a fee by link) applies when there is a link host and the normalised message also contains an entry from each of deliveryParcelWords, deliveryHoldWords and deliveryFeeWords. linkPatterns finds bare domains with a fixed TLD list, lowercase only. Link hosts get uppercase links because normalize() lowercases first. A case-insensitive flag is not an option: case-insensitive matching differs between ICU, Java and V8 for characters like U+017F. lookalikeLink (a link that copies a bank, government or company address) applies when a folded host, without its dots and hyphens, contains a lookalikeBrandTokens entry, or when one of its labels (the parts between dots and hyphens) is a lookalikeHostLabels entry, and the plain host is not an officialDomains entry or a subdomain of one. The plain host catches homoglyph spellings: "іtau.com.br" with a Cyrillic і and "bradesc0.com.br" fold to an official name but are not one. Tokens are not the reserved names: short names like inter, neon, pix and sus are inside common words and hosts. bankAlert (a fake bank alert: your account or Pix is blocked, fix it at this link) applies when there is a link host and the normalised message also contains an entry from bankAlertSubjectWords and from bankAlertThreatWords. lookalikeHostLabels are short public-body and bank names (bcb, gov, inss, receita, detran, bb) that are too short to match inside a host: "valoresareceber-bcb.site" warns, "receitas.globo.com" does not. Whole-word lists (remoteAppInstallWords, remoteAppNames, pinRequestSecretWords, pinRequestSupportWords) match like family terms: each run of characters outside [0-9a-z] in the normalised message becomes one space, then the term must have a space on each side. extortion (a threat with a payment demand: sextortion, "I know where you live") applies when the normalised message contains an extortionThreatPhrases entry and an extortionDemandWords entry. A threat without a payment demand is not this kind. remoteApp (a request to install a remote-access app) applies when the message has a remoteAppInstallWords entry and either a remoteAppNames entry, or a link host whose plain host is not an officialDomains or appStoreDomains entry or a subdomain of one together with a remoteAppBankWords entry. pinRequest (fake Bipe support asks for the PIN or a code) applies when the normalised message contains a pinRequestAskPhrases entry, a pinRequestSecretWords entry and a pinRequestSupportWords entry.

homoglyphs.$comment: Character folding applied after lowercasing and diacritic stripping, before comparing display names with reserved names and contacts (security.md rule 8). Starter set covering common Cyrillic, Greek and leetspeak substitutions. A full Unicode confusables table replaces this before launch.

handles.$comment: Username (handle) rules, docs/usernames.md layer 2. The skeleton is normalize(handle) with separators removed; two handles with the same skeleton cannot both exist. ASCII-explicit pattern, portable to ICU, java.util.regex and V8. ownerMinLength: a handle shorter than minLength is valid only when it is a key of handles in reserved-name-owners.json (ADR 0065).

suggestions.$comment: Escolha seu @ (bipe-chat/bipe#200): handleSuggestions(displayName) gives up to candidates handles of the right shape, in order; the app checks availability in that order and shows the first shown that are free. Rule and order: tools/lib/registries.mjs handleSuggestions, test-vectors/handle-suggestions.json.

owners.$comment: Who may use each reserved name. owners (ADR 0042): key is a normalised name from reserved-names.json, value is the CNPJ roots (first 8 characters) allowed to use it. Staff add an entry only after approving a claim from a CNPJ-verified account. A reserved name with no entry here is usable by nobody. handles (ADR 0065): key is a handle that is its own skeleton, value is the Matrix user ID that alone may hold that handle or any handle with the same skeleton. Only these handles may be shorter than handles.json minLength (down to ownerMinLength). Every change is a reviewed commit. The apps get only the handle names.

officialAccounts.$comment: Official Bipe accounts (ADR 0117, ADR 0119, ADR 0133). Match the full Matrix user ID exactly for the Bipe badge. A display name, handle or lookalike ID is not proof. Handle ownership must match reserved-name-owners.json.

profiles.$comment: Public profile rules, ADR 0041 (bipe/docs/adr). The server is the authority; clients check early for feedback. The name is also checked against reserved-names.json (exact match after normalize()). sealLookalikeEmoji (security.md rule 8): marks that look like the verified seal and may not appear in a display name. Compare after removing the variation selectors U+FE0E and U+FE0F from the name and the entry; an entry is found when it is a substring of the name. socials (ADR 0228): the networks a public profile may link to, in display order. The user types a handle, never a URL. pattern: the whole handle after socialHandleClean() (trim, one leading @), case-insensitive by its character classes. url: https only, {handle} once.

inviteCodes.$comment: Invite codes. extractInviteCode(text): uppercase the first maxInputLength characters; find the first match of pattern; join the three groups with '-'. No match: null. Alphabet ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789 (no 0/O, 1/I/L), same as bipe-api newInviteCode(). Separators between groups: none, one space, or one hyphen or dash (U+002D, U+2010 to U+2014, U+2212). Portable: ICU (Swift), java.util.regex (Kotlin), V8 (JS). Cases: test-vectors/invite-codes.json.

phones.$comment: Phone numbers for contact discovery (bipe/docs/usernames.md layer 5). normalizePhone(text): drop every '(0)' (the European trunk notation '+31 (0)6 ...'); keep a leading '+' and the digits of the first maxInputLength characters; '00' at the start means '+'. With '+' and countryCode: the rest must be a Brazilian mobile (below). With '+' and another country code: accepted as written when the digits are internationalMinDigits to internationalMaxDigits long and do not start with 0 (E.164; no per-country check). Without '+': Brazilian only. Drop a trunk prefix '0' plus a two-digit carrier code (0 + carrier + area + subscriber), or a bare trunk '0', or a leading countryCode, to reach area code + subscriber. Brazilian mobile: the area code must be in areaCodes; the subscriber must be mobileLength digits starting with mobilePrefix. Result: '+' and the digits, or null. Brazilian landlines and numbers without a country or area code are null. Cases: test-vectors/phone-numbers.json. Yearly confirmation (bipe-chat/bipe#470, bipe/docs/phone-link.md): a linked number stays findable for linkConfirmMonths after its last proof (confirmed_at); lookup skips it after that. The apps warn linkConfirmWarnDays before confirm_by. displayPhone(e164) (ADR 0191, bipe-chat/bipe#787, #788): formats an E.164 number for reading. The first display entry whose countryCode starts the digits, whose prefix (may be empty) starts the rest, and whose pattern has one # per digit of the rest gives '+' countryCode, a space, then the rest put into the pattern. No entry fits: the E.164 number as it is. Any other text comes back unchanged. Cases: test-vectors/phone-numbers.json display.

bipeServers.$comment: Bipe homeservers (ADR 0168, bipe-chat/bipe#680). A Bipe user is a Matrix user ID whose server name is in servers: '@' + a non-empty localpart + ':' + a server name that equals an entry exactly. The server name is everything after the first ':' (a port stays part of it, so 'bipe.net.br:8448' is another server). Entries are lower case. Rule: isBipeUserID in tools/lib/registries.mjs; cases: test-vectors/bipe-servers.json. The signed operator list replaces this bundled list in bipe-chat/bipe#682.

regions.$comment: Bipe regions (bipe ADR 0197). A region is what a chartered association covers. A core serves one region. An account's region comes from the server name of its user ID: each server in registries/bipe-servers.json belongs to exactly one region. floor: 'e2ee' federates with other regions, 'none' runs alone. The signed operator list (bipe-chat/bipe#645) adds operators under each region.

accounts.$comment: Device-first accounts: ADR 0057 and ADR 0059 (bipe/docs/adr), security.md rules 5 and 6. PIN rule, reference pinProblem() in tools/lib/registries.mjs, cases in test-vectors/pins.json. A PIN is exactly pinLength ASCII digits. It is weak when all digits are the same (repeated_digit), when each digit is the previous digit plus 1 or minus 1 modulo 10 (sequence: 12345678, 87654321, 90123456), or when it is a real calendar date as DDMMYYYY or YYYYMMDD with the year from pinDateYearMin to pinDateYearMax (date). Check order: not_digits, wrong_length, repeated_digit, sequence, date. pinMaxWrongTries: wrong PINs in total, over every recovery path, before the server blocks the PIN until a reset; a correct PIN sets the count to 0. recoveryDelayHours: wait between the factor plus PIN and access (or the new PIN). guardianApprovalsMax: approvals needed = min(guardians, guardianApprovalsMax). recoveryLinkMinutes: life of the recovery link in the email. emailVerifyLinkHours: life of the link that confirms a fallback email. recoveryClaimDays: after the delay ends, the new device has this long to collect the result. Linked recovery (ADR 0096): providers are recovery factors, need the existing PIN after provider proof, wait 24 hours, and cannot reset a PIN. One account of each provider per Bipe account. flowMinutes: life of a link nonce, of a web flow and of its handoff. maxPersonalAccounts (ADR 0086): personal accounts one phone holds at most. Company accounts do not count. The API returns the live cap as max_accounts in GET /v1/me/account; this value is the fallback when the app has no answer. webLinkCooldownSeconds (ADR 0116, ADR 0118, security.md rule 5): the wait on the phone after the full-access warning and before the biometric check that approves a web sign-in by QR code. Keep it short: the Synapse rendezvous session lives 60 seconds from the QR code, and the whole approval must fit in it. recoveryReminder (bipe#531, bipe/docs/team-transfer-recovery.md section 5): the recovery-reminder card shows for an account without a Team-ID-independent factor (independent_recovery false) from firstAfterDays after the account came to this phone. Each "Agora não" hides it for the next value of snoozeDays; the last value repeats, so the card never stops for good while the account has no factor. Account deletion (ADR 0140): deletionCooldownHours is the wait between the request and the deletion; every signed-in device can cancel during it. deletionVerificationKeepDays: after a deletion the server keeps only the CPF hash and the badge record for this long, so a deleted account cannot verify again at once to get around a block (bipe-chat/bipe#528). Approval nudge (bipe-chat/bipe#628, spec device-verification): a new phone that waits for approval can send the nudge push again after approvalNudgeAgainSeconds; the server sends at most approvalNudgeMaxPerHour nudges per account.

legal.$comment: Terms of use and privacy policy that a person accepts to create an account (clickwrap, ADR 0113 in bipe/docs/adr). version names the pair of texts in bipe-web src/legal (termos.md, privacidade.md, terms.md, privacy.md) as their date, YYYY-MM-DD. Change version in the same change that changes the meaning of either text; the bipe-web git history at that commit is the record of what each version said. The apps send version with POST /v1/signup and POST /v1/me/terms; the server refuses any other value. termsPath and privacyPath are paths on PUBLIC_SITE_URL, pt first; enTermsPath and enPrivacyPath for English. homePath and enHomePath are the site home pages that onboarding-welcome learnMore opens.

agendaTemplates.$comment: Editable suggestions for Ativar agenda (bipe#317, ADRs 0099-0103). Stable IDs. Times use the business time zone; omitted weekdays are closed. Prices start on request. Copy lives in strings only.

growth.$comment: Server-side growth events (ADR 0098 in bipe/docs/adr, bipe#67). The apps send no telemetry: the Bipe API derives each event from what the server already sees. It keeps a row per pseudonymous user (HMAC-SHA256 of the Matrix ID under BIPE_GROWTH_HMAC_SECRET), event and day, with a count. No event carries content, room IDs, Matrix IDs, IPs or devices. The platform events (ADR 0124) keep only ios, android or web: never the user agent, the model or the OS version. source: api = a Bipe API action; synapse_db = read from the Synapse database by the read-only role bipe_growth, which has SELECT only on the columns that bipe-api src/growth.ts names (no event content, no IP, no device name). once: the API keeps only the first day per user. funnel: the steps of the report, in order; a user counts at a step only with every earlier step. retentionEvent and retentionDays: the report shows the share of each sign-up week with retentionEvent on day N after sign-up. retentionDaysKept: rows older than this are deleted. A new event needs a line here, not a new ADR.

events.detail: POST /v1/signup made the account (a row in signups). A replayed sign-up (ADR 0094) does not count again.
The first authenticated GET /v1/me/account after signup_done: the app holds its credentials and is signed in.
The first m.room.message or m.room.encrypted event from the user (events: sender, type, origin_server_ts). Only the type is read.

The user signed another user's cross-signing key (e2e_cross_signing_signatures: user_id, target_user_id). n = new contacts. Synapse keeps no time for a signature, so the day is the day the API first sees it.
POST /v1/me/invites made a personal invite. n = invites made that day.
Counted for the inviter: a sign-up used one of the user's personal invites. n = sign-ups that day.

The user sent m.room.create for a room that is not a space and has 3 or more members, or 2 or more members and a room name (room_stats_current, room_stats_state.room_type, current_state_events type only). The name itself is not read. Day = day of m.room.create.

The user sent a call event (m.call.invite, m.call.member, org.matrix.msc3401.call.member) in a room with no call event in the hour before. Only type, room and time are read; the room ID is not kept. Approximation: a leave more than an hour after the last call event counts again.
The user sent any event that day, or sent a read receipt (receipts_linearized: user_id, stream_id; day = day the API sees it). A push that only wakes the app does not count.

A device of the user was last seen that day with an iOS app user agent (devices: user_id, user_agent, last_seen; not display_name, not ip). The API reads the user agent, keeps only the platform and drops the string. n = 1. Rule: a user agent with Mozilla/ is web; else iOS, iPhone, iPad or macOS is ios (the iOS app on a Mac counts as ios); else Android is android; else no event.
A device of the user was last seen that day with an Android app user agent. Same source and rule as platform_ios. n = 1.
A device of the user was last seen that day with a browser user agent (Element Web at chat.bipe.net.br). Same source and rule as platform_ios. n = 1.

The day the user got a fifth contact (bipe-chat/bipe#752). A contact is another local person who shares a DM with the user: a room that is not a space, has no room name, 2 joined members, no invited member, and m.room.member events from exactly those 2 people (room_stats_current, room_stats_state.room_type, current_state_events type, events sender, type, room_id and origin_server_ts only). The day of a contact is the day of the first member event of the person who came second. Only that day is kept: not the contacts, not the rooms, not the count.
GET /v1/me/business/setup answered with a step not done (ADR 0194). One event per account and day; no step ID and no record content.
The server computed a setup step as done for the first time for this account (ADR 0194).
PUT /v1/me/business/sector with no sector (Pular) on an account that never had one (ADR 0194).
A booking made on the web with a shop token (ADR 0195). No name and no shop.
An order made on the web with a shop token (ADR 0195). No name and no shop.
A signed-in person claimed the records of a shop token (ADR 0195).

trust.$comment: ADR 0074: separate identity proof, personal confirmation, lifecycle changes and the already-selected warning. Facts only; no trust score or safe classification. Times are Unix seconds. Source adapters must establish complete authenticated lifecycle data before setting lifecycleKnown.

settings.$comment: Settings structure (ADR 0112 in bipe/docs/adr). One source for the order of groups, sections and rows on iOS and Android. `root` is the order of the group rows under Configurações in the Você tab; `profile` opens from the Você header; since 3 Nov 2026 it is one screen (product/screens/profile-edit) and lists no rows here. `icon` is the Phosphor icon (bipe-app tools/phosphor.json) of a root group row: a glyph in ink.onAccent on an accent.fill tile, as in the iPhone Settings app. A group with `screen: "element"` keeps the Element screen and lists no rows here. Row kinds: link (opens a screen), choice (opens a picker), switch, info (a value, no action), url (opens a page from `urls`), action (runs something), destructive. `gate`: absent = always shown; `ios` or `android` = that platform only; `flag:<name>` = behind that app feature flag; `planned:<issue>` = hidden until bipe-chat/bipe#<issue> ships. Titles are bipe_* string keys; a row without its own string has no place here. A new top-level group needs a new ADR.

onboarding.$comment: First run for new and returning users (bipe-chat/bipe#415, ADR 0072, ADR 0113). One source for the start screen, the sign-up steps, the recovery rows and the later prompts on iOS and Android. `start`: the start screen variant per state; exactly one variant matches each pair of `invitePending` (an invite came from a link or a deferred install) and `inviteRequired` (GET /v1/signup/config). Every screen has one `primary` (filled) button and zero or more `text` buttons. `to` is a step key, `recovery`, `waitlist` or `create` (POST /v1/signup). `steps` are the sign-up screens in order. `recovery` rows are in screen order; `when` names the state that shows a row; `gate` is `planned:<issue>` for a row that stays hidden until bipe-chat/bipe#<issue> ships. `apple` and `google` (ADR 0096) show only when GET /v1/links/providers offers a path for that provider on the platform (Apple native on iOS, else web). `prompts` come after the account exists; `trigger` says when. `afterDaysOnPhone` (bipe#125): the account is osTheftProtection.afterDays old on this phone. `withoutPhoto`: the account has no avatar. `messageSent`: the account sent a message on this phone and the system notification permission was never asked. Every prompt but bringPeople (a sheet) is an entry of chatListPrompt: no prompt has a place of its own (bipe-chat/bipe#894, MZ 2 Nov 2026). `chatListWithoutRecovery` (bipe#531): GET /v1/me/account says independent_recovery false, the account is at least accounts.json recoveryReminder.firstAfterDays old on this phone and the snooze ended; the handle card goes first, one card at a time (spec recovery-reminder). Titles and bodies are bipe_* string keys.

promptSlot.$comment: Every ask of the app shares one slot per account (bipe-chat/bipe#200, bipe-chat/bipe#894): after one shows, no other shows for hours. The same ask may keep showing in its slot. A dismissed ask comes back only when its source says when.

pinReminder.$comment: Trigger pinReminderDue (bipe-chat/bipe#202), spaced like Signal: the gap after step n is days[n], then thenEveryDays. A right PIN goes one step on; a wrong PIN goes back to step 0; Agora não keeps the step and asks again after 1 day. The first reminder comes days[0] after this phone first saw the account. Rule: tools/lib/registries.mjs pinReminderNext, test-vectors/onboarding-schedule.json.

osTheftProtection.$comment: Trigger afterDaysOnPhone (bipe-chat/bipe#125, ADR 0045 tier 0): the chatListPrompt entry osTheftProtection is eligible once the account is afterDays old on this phone (the first time this phone saw it). Agora não, or the button, hides it for good on this phone, for every account. The button target osTheftSettings opens the phone's settings (iOS UIApplication.openSettingsURLString; Android Settings.ACTION_SECURITY_SETTINGS on Samsung, else Settings.ACTION_SETTINGS). Neither OS lets an app read whether its theft protection is on (spec theft-protection notes), so the app never says it is on.

bringPeople.$comment: Specs bring-people and bring-people-reminder (bipe-chat/bipe#752, MZ 26 Oct 2026). Trigger firstChatListAfterSignup: the account signed up on this phone, Conversas shows with no chat open and no other sheet, and the sheet never showed on this account. It opens once with `slots` slots for the `firstCircle` circle (ADR 0047). Trigger bringPeopleDue: at least followUpEveryDays since the last ask, fewer than stopAfterDeclines declines, and a slot pending for at least pendingAfterDays or expired; the oldest such slot is named. Agora não on the sheet (no slot filled) or on the reminder adds one decline. Rule: tools/lib/registries.mjs bringPeopleReminder, test-vectors/onboarding-schedule.json.

chatListPrompt.$comment: The one ask system of the app (spec chat-list-prompt, bipe-chat/bipe#894, MZ 2 Nov 2026): one queue, one place (the first row of the chat list), one slot per account. In queue order, the first entry whose source condition holds and that the slot allows shows. tier critical and access preempt the slot; every other entry waits promptSlot.hours after the last card left. Keys equal to a prompts key keep that prompt's dismiss memory. The bring-people sheet (prompts.bringPeople) is the only ask that is not an entry; it claims the slot when it opens. Full-screen alerts (recovery-alert, deletion-alert, device-verification incoming, incoming calls) are not asks: they interrupt at once and never use the slot.

firstList.$comment: Cards at the top of Conversas while it lists at most maxChats chats (bipe-chat/bipe#198, spec chat-list-cards). A card goes away for good once used or dismissed. `when`: hasHandle shows the card only while the account has an @; bringPeopleNotShown shows it only while the bring-people sheet never showed on this account (MZ, 2 Nov 2026: the sheet and its reminder do the asking, so the invite card is for accounts that never saw the sheet).

haptics.$comment: Bipe haptics language (ADR 0134 in bipe/docs/adr; design: bipe/docs/design/haptics.md). Eight haptics, named by what they mean, not by how they feel. App code plays a haptic by id (iOS BipeHaptics.play(.tick), Android view.bipeHaptic(BipeHaptic.Tick)) and never calls a platform feedback API directly. ios: the UIKit generator and its argument. android: HapticFeedbackConstants names in order of preference; the app plays the first one whose minSdk is at or below the device API level. uses: where the apps play the haptic today; the parity ledger checks the same list. A new use needs a line here, not a new ADR. A new haptic needs a new ADR.

haptics.meaning: A choice changed: a tab, a segment, a picker value, a reaction or poll answer toggled, an emoji picked.
A press did a real thing at once: a message sent, text copied, the timeline jumped to the newest message.
A drag crossed the point where letting go acts: swipe to reply, swipe to archive.
The same drag went back under the point: letting go now does nothing.
A long press took hold: a message menu opened, a voice recording started. A system context menu plays its own haptic; Bipe adds none.
Something the user set up or waited for finished well: a PIN set, the app unlocked, a verification done, an invite made.
Bipe asks the user to stop and look before going on, in a flow the user started: a Pix check found a risk, the full-access warning before a web sign-in.
An action the user took failed at once: a wrong PIN.

badgeKeys.$comment: Badge signing keys the apps trust (docs/badge-attestation.md, bipe ADR 0123). kid to raw Ed25519 public key, base64url without padding. Only public keys. The private key is made on the cluster and never leaves it (bipe-infra scripts/setup-badge-key.sh prints the public key). Never list a test-only-* kid here. lifeDays: badge life from iat to exp. renewDaysBeforeExpiry: the API signs a new badge when the cached one has less life than this.

clearedChats.$comment: Cleared DMs (bipe-chat/bipe#464). "Apagar conversa" in a DM keeps the user in the room and writes a marker in the global account data event below: { "rooms": { "<room_id>": { "ts": <ms> } } }. ts is the origin_server_ts of the latest event in the room when the user cleared it. The chat list hides the DM while its latest event ts is at or below the marker. The timeline and search drop every event at or below the marker. A malformed entry counts as not cleared. A write merges into the event and keeps every other entry. Reference implementation: clearedChat* in tools/lib/registries.mjs; cases: test-vectors/cleared-chats.json.

chatFavourites.$comment: Favourites order (spec chat-list, MZ 3 Nov 2026). The favourites row shows in the order the user sets. The global account data event below holds it: { "rooms": ["<room_id>", ...] }, first room first. The m.favourite tag stays the source of which chats are favourites; this list only orders them. The SDK can write the m.favourite tag order but cannot read it back (matrix-sdk-ffi 26.08.11 has Room.setIsFavourite(tagOrder) and no getter), so the order lives here. Display: favourites in the list come first, in list order; favourites not in the list follow, by name (case-insensitive), then room ID. A room ID that is no longer a favourite stays in the list and has no effect. A new favourite goes last. Removing a favourite removes its room ID. A reorder in one scope keeps the positions of the other scope's rooms. A write keeps the first orderMax room IDs; a favourite past the limit shows by name. A malformed event counts as an empty list. A failed write keeps the order on this phone and writes again at the next change.

imageDescriptions.$comment: Image descriptions (alt text, bipe-chat/bipe#501). The sender writes an optional description of a photo in upload-preview. It travels in the content of the m.image event as the top-level string field below, next to body and filename, inside the encrypted event. Readers take it only from an m.image event: a non-string or blank value counts as none, and text after maxLength characters is dropped. VoiceOver and TalkBack read it before the caption (timeline-media, media-viewer). Matrix has no stable alt-text field yet; when one lands, apps send both and read the stable one first.

pixMarks.$comment: Pix request marks (ADR 0046, bipe-chat/bipe#130). Bipe is not in the money path (ADR 0012): "pago" comes from two marks on the request card, never from bank data. A mark is a room event of eventType whose content has m.relates_to {rel_type: relType, event_id: <the card event>}, mark (one of marks), payer (the payer's user ID: the line of a split card; may be left out on a card with one payer) and, on sent only, e2e_id (the payer's claim from the bank receipt, format e2eIdPattern: E, the 8-digit ISPB, 23 letters or digits). Only the payer of the line marks sent; only the requester (the card's sender) marks received or not_received. Transitions per line, from issued: sent from issued, sent or not_received; received from issued, sent or not_received; not_received from sent or received. Marks are read in origin_server_ts order, ties by event ID. A mark that breaks a rule is rejected and never changes a line; every accepted mark stays in the line history, so a correction shows both events. A line is paid only in state received. The BR Code txid of a card is its request ID: letters and digits only, at most txidMaxLength. Reference implementation: pixMarkLines and pixTxid in tools/lib/pix.mjs; cases: test-vectors/pix-marks.json.

dataUse.$comment: Data use (bipe-chat/bipe#242). On most prepaid plans data for some messaging apps is free and data for Bipe is not, so Bipe keeps a budget for a normal day and light defaults. budgetMegabytesPerDay is an estimate from the sizes below (UNVERIFIED until MZ measures a normal day on an iPhone and an Android phone, 25 Oct 2026): text and sync about 2.5 MB (200 messages, receipts, typing, one group), 10 voice messages sent or received (30 s Opus at 32 kbit/s, about 120 kB each: 1.2 MB), 5 photos sent at standard quality (2048 px JPEG, about 450 kB each: 2.25 MB), 10 photos received as thumbnails (about 40 kB each: 0.4 MB) and 5 of them opened full size (2.25 MB): about 8.6 MB, rounded up to 10. Defaults: videos and voice messages download only on a tap or play; a received photo shows its thumbnail and loads the full file only in the viewer; photos and videos are sent at standard quality (upload-preview). dataSaver (the switch bipe_data_use_saver, and also the system Low Data Mode on iOS or Data Saver on Android): on mobile data, photo and sticker thumbnails wait for a tap. The counters of data-use count only media Bipe sent or downloaded on the phone, split by mobile data and Wi-Fi; they stay on the phone and roll over each calendar month.

brandMarks.$comment: Brand marks for resellers (bipe ADR 0162, bipe-chat/bipe#483). A verified brand (CNPJ seal) grants a mark to a reseller's work account through a single-use invite; the reseller accepts. labels: the fixed words, one string key each (bipe_brand_mark_label_<id>, argument: the brand's name); the brand picks one, no free text. maxPerAccount: active marks one work account holds. inviteDays: life of an unused invite. recheckMinutes: how long the apps keep a fetched mark before they ask again (the same as the CNPJ seal), so a revoked mark goes from customers' phones within that time. The envelope is a badge of lvl brand-mark (docs/badge-attestation.md), life lifeDays of registries/badge-keys.json.

businessTools.$comment: Business tools and the step-by-step path of the Trabalho tab (ADR 0194, bipe-chat/bipe#798). Stable IDs. needs: a real dependency; catalog_service and catalog_product mean at least one active catálogo item of that kind. A tool with no needs is never blocked. steps: the done rule is computed by bipe-api from records. sectors: step_order is the order the sector sets, first_tool the first tool the tab suggests, agenda_template an ID of agenda-templates.json (or absent). A sector never limits the tools (ADR 0194 point 9). generic: the path of an account with no sector. suggestions: rules on records only, never on chats (ADR 0194 points 14 to 16). resale: the sector that shows Selos de revenda in the tab (ADR 0194 point 19).

at least catalogMinItems active catálogo items
at least one tool is live
a verified CNPJ claim; an autônomo with no CNPJ does not get this step (ADR 0138)
the account has a second seat

an active catálogo service, and the tool is off
an active catálogo product with a fixed amount, and the tool is off

voiceMedia.$comment: Voice message audio expiry (ADR 0164, bipe-chat/bipe#622). After the upload, the sending app registers the media ID of a voice message with the API (PUT /v1/me/voice-media). The API deletes the file from the media repository transcriptDays after the upload when the message has a transcript, noTranscriptDays after it when it has none. The event and the transcript stay. Media that nobody registered never expires. Any account can keep a voice message's audio (PUT /v1/me/kept-media), up to maxKeptPerAccount; kept audio never expires while one account keeps it. The app keeps an incoming voice message with a scam warning by itself (reason scam). maxKeptPerAccount 200 is a default (about 36 MB of one-minute 24 kbit/s audio per account); MZ can overrule it. Forward marks (bipe-chat/bipe#83): a forward from a Bipe app adds the top-level object forwardKey with an integer count to the copied content: the count of the original plus 1, or 1 when the original has none. A count of forwardedManyTimes or more shows the many-times line on a voice message or audio file. A missing or malformed mark counts as 0 and means no forward line, never proof that the message was not forwarded: a modified app can drop or fake the mark. forwardedManyTimes 5 is a default (the threshold people know from other messengers); MZ can overrule it. Every forwarded message of any kind with a count of 1 or more shows a forward line (bipe-chat/bipe#933): forwarded, or forwardedManyTimes at the threshold. A forward goes to at most forwardChats chats; when a content it sends has a count of forwardedManyTimes or more (the original count plus 1), it goes to at most forwardChatsManyTimes chats, the brake other messengers put on chain messages. forwardChats 5 and forwardChatsManyTimes 1 are defaults; MZ can overrule them.

stickers.$comment: Stickers (bipe ADR 0029, ADR 0033, ADR 0205; bipe-chat/bipe#837). import: the limits for a file that sticker-import or sticker-from-photo adds to a pack, also animated WebP; a WhatsApp animated sticker fits. made: the size of a sticker that Bipe makes (sticker-from-photo now, a GIF from a video later); madeAnimatedMaxMilliseconds is ADR 0205's 3 seconds. Recents and favourites are global account data, lists of { pack, shortcode }, newest first, capped. tagsField is a list of tag ids on an image of an MSC2545 pack. packField on an m.sticker event names its pack room ({ room_id, state_key }), only when the pack is a room pack. Search (rules: stickerSearchFold, stickerQueryTags, stickerMatches in tools/lib/registries.mjs; test-vectors/sticker-search.json) runs on the phone only. words and emoji map a folded word or an emoji to tag ids. A word key is already folded: lower case, no accents, every run of one repeated letter cut to one letter, so kkkk is k and aff is af. An emoji key has no variation selector and no skin tone. Every tag id also matches itself as a word.

maps.$comment: Maps for location sharing (ADR 0131, bipe-chat/bipe#768). Every map request goes to baseUrl, our tile server in Brazil; no other map service and no API key. staticPath is the tileserver-gl static map: the app replaces {style}, {lon}, {lat}, {zoom}, {width} and {height} (points; the server renders @2x). width and height stay at or under maxStaticSize. The server draws the attribution into each image. defaultZoom: a new pin and a received location without zoom_level. coordinateDecimals: digits after the point in the geo URI (6 is about 0.1 m). detailBounds (west, south, east, north) is the area the server has at every zoom, the same box as bipe-infra maps.yaml; outside it the server has the world only to zoom 6, so a map centred outside detailBounds goes no deeper than outsideMaxZoom. live (MSC3489 live location): durationsMinutes are the choices of the send screen (under 60 shown as minutes, else hours). The app sends a new position when the phone moved at least the chosen distance (distancesMetres, setting chats.liveLocation, default defaultDistanceMetres), at most every minIntervalSeconds, and while it moves at least every maxIntervalSeconds.

voiceTranscript.$comment: Paragraphs in a voice message transcript (bipe/docs/audio.md, ADR 0023). The recogniser gives one long run of text. The phone splits it into paragraphs before the sender sees it, on both platforms, with the rule in product/screens/voice-recording.json notes. pauseSeconds: a silence this long between two words starts a new paragraph when the paragraph has at least minCharacters and the text before the silence ends a sentence; a silence of twice pauseSeconds starts one also without a sentence end. maxCharacters: a paragraph this long ends at its next sentence end, with or without a silence. The values are first guesses (UNVERIFIED, 25 Oct 2026): MZ checks them by hand on real áudios.

homeScore.$comment: Mural home score (ADR 0246, bipe-chat/bipe#1044; spec chat-list). One pure function of explicit inputs. The phone computes it and sends nothing. Weights are first values, not measured. U(x) = floor(x * 10000 + 0.5): a score part in integer units of 1/10000. Every log and exp term goes through U before the sum, so a last-bit difference between libm versions does not reach the result. Sum these parts as integers. mentioned: U(weights.mention). Direct chat (kind person or company) with unreadCount > 0: U(weights.unreadDirect), or U(weights.unreadCompanyNoSeal) when kind is company and hasSeal is false. Group with unreadCount > 0: min(U(unreadGroup.max), U(unreadGroup.min + unreadGroup.logScale * log10(1 + unreadCount))). Direct chat with unreadCount = 0, lastFromOther true and minutesSinceActivity known and below unansweredMaxMinutes: U(weights.unansweredDirect). favourite: U(weights.favourite). Every chat: min(U(tie.max), U(tie.logScale * log2(1 + messagesPerWeek))). Known minutesSinceActivity: U(recency.max * exp(-minutes / recency.decayMinutes)); half-life about 5.5 hours. Model part: 0 when kind is company without a seal, official is true or trustWarning is true. Else U(model.attention[modelAttention]) when the value is known, and for none only when unreadCount > 0, plus U(model.due) when modelDue is true, at most U(model.maxWeight). An unknown attention value adds 0. Then, in this order: muted and not mentioned: S = floor(S * mutedFactor + 0.5). official: S = min(S, U(officialCap)). Clamp S to 0...10000. scorePercent P = floor((S + 50) / 100). score = P / 100. Negative minutesSinceActivity, unreadCount and messagesPerWeek count as 0. Null minutesSinceActivity means unknown. Order: P descending, then minutesSinceActivity ascending with unknown last, then room ID ascending by code unit. Tier: walk the chats in that order. Each chat takes the first tier where P >= minScore * 100 and the tier is below maxChats (null: no limit). A full tier demotes the chat to the next. A chat past tier 4 gets no tile (tier null) and stays in the plain list. The caller passes joined, not archived chats only: a request or an archived chat gets no score. Reference: tools/lib/home-score.mjs. Vectors: test-vectors/home-score.json. model: unused in step 1, callers pass no model fields until step 3 of ADR 0246 passes its gate.

dmSelection.$comment: ADR 0141: choose one eligible joined DM per person before unread/name filtering. Exclude cleared rooms for lists/search and ordinary Start chat. When all existing DMs are cleared, Start chat reuses the newest existing room so it never creates a duplicate; timelines retain their clear markers. Greatest latest-event timestamp wins, missing timestamps last, ascending room ID on ties. Never delete rooms or merge histories.

dmPowerLevels.$comment: ADR 0141, bipe-chat/bipe#532: the m.room.power_levels content of a new DM. Both people sit at usersDefault, so neither can invite, kick, ban, delete the other person's messages or change the room (name, photo, topic, power levels, join rules, history, encryption). Messages, reactions, deleting own messages, call membership and the assistant notice stay at 0. The assistant notice is the state event chat.bipe.assistant that a member's own assistant writes to read the whole chat (bipe ADR 0130, bipe-chat/bipe#879); its state key is the sender's user ID, so a member can set only their own. Clients create the room with the user at createLevel and the other person at 0, so that the server can write the first state and the invite, then send this content. Old DMs keep their power levels.

groupPowerLevels.$comment: bipe-chat/bipe#733: the three roles of a group and the m.room.power_levels of a new group. Admin changes roles and group settings and notifies everyone with @room (#718). Moderador removes and bans members, deletes other people's messages and pins messages. Membro posts, reacts and replies. The app shows no numbers and no custom levels. A room whose levels another Matrix app changed keeps them: the members screen shows the nearest role and a note. The assistant notice chat.bipe.assistant stays open, as in DMs (bipe-chat/bipe#879). Old groups keep their power levels.

relationshipNames.$comment: ADR 0018: compare only a known saved contact name with an authenticated verified name. Normalise both with the shared normaliser. A differing full name warns; a family label or one-word nickname asks once per saved-label/verified-identity pair. A confirmation never clears a full-name mismatch. No name is proof of identity and this rule makes no safety claim.

photoMatch.$comment: ADR 0049, security rule 15: on-device photo match. Each app keeps a perceptual hash of each contact's avatar and warns when a non-contact's avatar matches one. No image or hash leaves the phone. Method dhash: draw the avatar into a width x height grayscale grid (luma 0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B, rounded, 0..255; area-average scaling, no aspect-ratio crop beyond the centre square the avatar already is), then bit (y * (width - 1) + x) is 1 when gray[y][x] < gray[y][x + 1]. The 64 bits are written as 16 lowercase hex digits, bit 0 first (most significant). Two avatars match when the Hamming distance of their hashes is at most maxDistance. Reference: photoHash, photoDistance, photoMatches in tools/lib/registries.mjs; cases in test-vectors/photo-match.json. The threshold is a working default (ADR 0049 leaves it open until there is real data).

profileFacts.$comment: Account age and profile change facts, ADR 0049 (bipe/docs/adr, security.md rule 15, bipe-chat/bipe#598). The API keeps the dates of display-name and photo changes (Matrix profile and public profile) for windowDays and serves them with the account creation time (POST /v1/profile-facts). The apps show the lines of profileFactLines() (tools/lib/registries.mjs, test-vectors/profile-facts.json) on chat-request and person-profile: the account age only when the account is younger than newAccountDays; per kind, one change shows its age, more changes show their count in windowDays. Nothing when nothing applies. noticePairHours and noticeDays: a contact whose name change and photo change lie at most noticePairHours apart gets the amber notice in the chat while the later of the two is younger than noticeDays.

reach.$comment: First-contact outcomes for reach reputation (security.md rule 11, bipe-chat/bipe#39, bipe-chat/bipe#845). A first contact is an invite that the API allows when the inviter and the invitee share no other joined room and no invite pair (bipe-api mayInvite). The API keeps one row per first contact: the inviter, a keyed hash of the invitee, the room and the time, for recipientDays. In that time the Synapse module bipe_messaging reports the invitee's join (accepted), the invitee's own leave from the invite (declined) and a new ignore of the inviter (blocked, only within blockWindowDays of the first contact). A row with no join or leave and no block after recipientDays counts as ignored; then the row goes. A user report (Synapse event_reports) counts against the sender of the reported event. The API keeps per-sender daily counts (sent, accepted, declined, ignored, blocked, reported) for dailyCountDays. Never a recipient ID in clear, never message content. Reach tiers and budget (bipe-chat/bipe#851): each tier has a budget of first contacts per rolling windowHours; GET /v1/me/reach returns it. Over the budget, the Synapse module refuses the invite with M_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. The budgets and the thresholds (new-account age, the slowed rule) are bipe-api environment configuration, not this file, because a public number is a target for abuse. Contacts and replies are never limited. tiers is the order of the contract enum ReachStatus.tier. recipientDays and blockWindowDays 7 come from the reach reputation strategy (27 October 2026, proposed); dailyCountDays 90 is a default; MZ can overrule.

theft.$comment: Theft protection, ADR 0044 and ADR 0051 (bipe/docs/adr, security.md rule 14, bipe-chat/bipe#600, #268). maxGuardians: guardians per account. markedMessageMinutes: messages from the marked account sent this long before stolen_at get the marker in contacts' chats. statementLifeHours: life of a signed theft statement (docs/theft-mark.md); the apps fetch again when it ends. checkMinutes: how often an app checks the marks of the people it shows, at most.

workHours.$comment: Work side opening hours (ADR 0138 rule 4, bipe-chat/bipe#511). A company account sets the hours of its work side on the phone; the API keeps them (GET and PUT /v1/me/work-hours) so every device of the account reads the same. Outside the hours, the phone shows the account's pushes without sound and without a banner, and keeps them in the notification list. The personal side never goes quiet because of the work side. Reference: isWithinWorkHours() in tools/lib/registries.mjs, cases in test-vectors/work-hours.json. days: ISO weekdays 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday); a day without a range is closed. A range is half-open [start, end) in local time HH:MM; end 24:00 means midnight; a range never crosses midnight (two ranges cover a night). At most maxRangesPerDay ranges per day, sorted, not touching. defaultTimeZone is used when the account has none. defaultDays is what a new work account starts with.

govbr.$comment: Trust step 5, Verificar com gov.br (bipe-chat/bipe#544, spec product/screens/govbr-verify.json). The apps send the user to the gov.br app to sign the challenge PDF of POST /v1/verifications/govbr. fileName is the GovbrChallenge fileName of api/openapi.yaml. maxDocumentBytes is the maxLength of PUT /v1/verifications/govbr/{verificationId}/document: the apps do not upload a bigger file. iosStoreUrl: the gov.br app has no documented URL scheme, so iOS opens its App Store page, which shows Abrir when the app is installed. androidPackage: Android opens the app by this package name when it is installed, else androidStoreUrl. Both store pages checked on 29 Oct 2026.

mcpTools.$comment: MCP tools of every Bipe MCP surface, one data class each (bipe ADR 0130, ADR 0210; bipe-chat/bipe#436). surface: bridge (bipe-business, the company's server), public (bipe-api, mcp.bipe.chat, Sao Paulo), personal (bipe-mcp on the user's machine). class: public (anyone can see it on bipe.chat, no opt-in), metadata (lists, assignees, tags, status, times; no text), content (message text, notes, attachments; off by default, opt-in per scope with the destination named). writes: none, draft (puts a draft in the user's apps, bipe#866), send (sends a message), state (changes status, tags or room state). A personal tool with writes send needs scope content-send, and bipe-mcp sends only while the user's switch is on: global account data personalSend.accountDataType {"enabled": true}, set from Settings on the phone, off by default (ADR 0210 as corrected by MZ on 30 October 2026). Every message it sends carries personalSend.markerField {"client": <MCP client name>}, and Bipe apps label it. A public tool has class public, writes none and no scope. The servers read this file; docs and the site render it. No second list. readerMarker: the room state event (state key = the member's own user ID) that bipe-mcp sets before it returns other members' messages (set_full_content); every member's app shows that the member's assistant reads the chat (assistantReaders, test-vectors/assistant-send.json).

drafts.$comment: Assistant drafts (bipe ADR 0210, bipe-chat/bipe#866; protocol: docs/drafts-room.md). Each account has one private, end-to-end encrypted drafts room with only the user's own devices. Its room ID is in global account data accountDataType as {"room_id": ...}; that ID, not the room type, identifies the room. The creating device sets the creation type roomType when its SDK can. A draft is an m.room.message with msgtype m.text in that room: body is the draft text, and the field named field holds {"room_id", "reply_to"?, "thread_root"?, "client"}. Other Matrix apps show the draft as plain text. The Bipe apps show a draft only when its sender is the user's own account and the target room is a joined room. Send and discard redact the draft message. bodyMaxLength and clientMaxLength cap what the apps show; a longer draft is ignored. Rules: test-vectors/drafts.json.

assistants.$comment: Assistants as chat members (bipe ADR 0210 point 1, bipe-chat/bipe#867). Any AI provider can run an assistant as a Bipe account. Staff register it with its operator, a company account with a verified CNPJ claim (ADR 0042); a foreign operator without a CNPJ needs a staff review before that (default chosen in ADR 0210). bipe-api answers GET /v1/assistants/{userId} (public) and POST /v1/assistants/resolve (up to maxResolve IDs, signed in). The apps show bipe_assistant_label on the profile and the member list, the operator and the model location (bipe_assistant_model_<location>), and bipe_assistant_joined when one joins a group. Only a group admin adds an assistant to a group. modelLocations: where the assistant's model runs, as the operator declares it.

ageSignals.$comment: Age signals, ADR 0229 (bipe/docs/adr): the age comes from the OS, never from a date of birth. The apps read Apple Declared Age Range (iOS, with appleGates) or Google Play Age Signals (Android Play build) and send the range to PUT /v1/me/age. The server maps the range to one band with ageBand() in tools/lib/registries.mjs and stores only the band. Rule: the band that holds the lowest age the range allows (lower, or 0 when lower is absent). No range is unknown. bands: in order, youngest first, each from min to max inclusive; the first has no min and the last no max. adultBand: the only band that does not get the under-18 defaults (unknown gets them too). recheckDays: the app reads the OS signal again when the server's age_checked_at is older than this. sources: where a range came from; none means the OS gave nothing (declined, no signal, foss build).

reportCategories.$comment: Report categories (bipe-chat/bipe#697, ADR 0170; design: Moderation in layers and trusted flaggers, sections 2, 5 and 6). A report carries one id. firstActionMinutes is the operator charter target from the report's arrival to the operator's first action (hide, suspend, or a decision to keep). flaggerEligible: an accredited trusted flagger may file this category. No political or disinformation category (ADR 0174). Strings: bipe_report_category_<id> (the name) and bipe_report_category_<id>_hint (one line under it). The sealed report format is docs/report-envelope.md. The order is the order of the report sheet. Values are defaults until the charter (#629) fixes them.

strings.$comment: Bipe-owned UI strings (Element strings stay on Localazy). DRAFT: not yet through the humanizer pass. Keys follow Element's naming rules with a bipe_ prefix. Placeholders use %1$s; generators convert per platform. No plural forms: a count goes into a placeholder that the platform formats with its own plural-aware formatter (bipe_banner_unverified_body %1$s = account age, for example '1 dia' or '2 dias', from DateComponentsFormatter / Android plurals). Words in a sentence never change with a count.

strings.bipe_year_recap_share_note: A imagem mostra só os números, sem nomes de pessoas ou conversas.

strings.bipe_group_link_joined_push_body: Alguém entrou num grupo seu pelo link. Toque para abrir o grupo.
strings.bipe_notifications_invite_joined: Quando alguém entra com meu convite
strings.bipe_notifications_group_link_joined: Quando alguém entra com meu link de grupo
strings.bipe_notifications_joins_footer: Vale para todos os seus aparelhos.
strings.bipe_web_signin_step_scan: Aponte a câmera do celular para este código.

strings.bipe_web_history_banner: Aprove este navegador para ler suas mensagens antigas.

strings.bipe_profile_notice_name_photo: %1$s changed their name and photo recently. Before you send money, check with them another way.
strings.bipe_theft_intro: Choose up to 3 people you trust. If your phone is stolen, any of them can mark your account as stolen. The account is signed out of every device at once.
strings.bipe_theft_guardians_footer: Only contacts you verified in person with the QR code can be guardians.
strings.bipe_theft_picker_empty: You have no verified contacts yet. Verify someone in person with the QR code and come back.
strings.bipe_theft_guarding_empty: Nobody chose you as a guardian yet.
strings.bipe_theft_mark_confirm_body: The account is signed out of every device at once and stays locked. Contacts see a warning. Do this only if %1$s asked you to, or you are sure the phone was stolen.
strings.bipe_theft_clear_confirm_body: The account works again. %1$s signs in again on a new device.
strings.bipe_theft_last_mark: Your account was marked as stolen by %1$s on %2$s.
strings.bipe_theft_error: That did not work now. Check your connection and try again.
strings.bipe_theft_banner_body: A guardian of %1$s marked this account as stolen. Do not send money or codes. Talk to them another way.
strings.bipe_theft_message_marker: Sent around the time of the theft
strings.bipe_banner_unverified_body: Account created %1$s ago. Not in your contacts.
strings.bipe_banner_external: Account from another service. Bipe doesn't verify this person's name.
strings.bipe_banner_security_change: This account signed in on a new device. Its name hasn't been verified on that device yet.
strings.bipe_warning_money_request_body: Before you pay, check with the person another way. Scammers rush you.
strings.bipe_warning_reserved_name: This name is reserved for verified organisations.
strings.bipe_warning_photo_match: This account uses the same photo as %1$s, who is in your chats.
strings.bipe_device_approval_never_for_others: Bipe never asks you to approve someone else's phone.
strings.bipe_badge_suspended_body: This account changed its encryption keys. The seal comes back when the person verifies their name again.
strings.bipe_badge_company_checked: Checked with the Receita Federal in
strings.bipe_badge_company_body: Bipe checked that the CNPJ is active at the Receita Federal and that this account belongs to the business. The seal does not vouch for every offer or charge. Before you pay, check the name your bank app shows.
strings.bipe_badge_company_revoked: This business is no longer verified.
strings.bipe_badge_company_revoked_not_active: This business is no longer verified. The CNPJ no longer shows as active at the Receita Federal.
strings.bipe_badge_company_suspended: This business's seal is suspended until Bipe checks the account again.
strings.bipe_brand_mark_body: The brand vouches for this account as its reseller. The brand does not read the chats and does not see the customers.
strings.bipe_brand_mark_brand_unchecked: We could not check the brand's seal right now.
strings.bipe_brand_mark_ended: %1$s no longer vouches for this reseller
strings.bipe_brand_marks_held_empty: No brand vouches for this account yet.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_held_footer: Customers see the mark next to your name. Your chats and customers stay yours.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_remove_confirm: Remove the mark of %1$s? Customers stop seeing it within 10 minutes. Your chats and customers stay with you.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_code_invalid: This code does not work. Ask the brand for a new one.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_offer_title: %1$s wants to vouch for this account
strings.bipe_brand_marks_brand_sees: The brand sees only that the mark is active.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_brand_not_sees: The brand does not see your chats, your customers or your contacts.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_limit: This account already has 3 marks. Remove one to accept another.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_already_held: This account already has this brand's mark.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_own_brand: A brand cannot give a mark to itself.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_failed: That did not work. Try again.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_grant_header: Give a mark to a reseller
strings.bipe_brand_marks_grant_footer: You pick the words of the mark. The reseller accepts it with the code. You see only that the mark is active.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_not_verified: Only a company with a verified seal can give reseller marks.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_code_ready: Send this code or link to the reseller. It works once, for %1$s days.
strings.bipe_brand_marks_end_confirm: End the mark of %1$s? Customers stop seeing it within 10 minutes.
strings.bipe_cvm_bank_note: A bank can sell CDBs and savings without a CVM registration.
strings.bipe_cvm_stop_order: CVM ordered this company to stop its offers on %1$s.
strings.bipe_cvm_stop_order_card: CVM ordered this company to stop its offers on %1$s. Do not invest or pay anything to it before you check the CVM website.
strings.bipe_claim_intro: Enter the company CNPJ. Bipe checks it with the Receita Federal and you prove that the company is yours. Then the account gets the verified business seal.
strings.bipe_claim_cnpj_invalid: This CNPJ is not right. Check the digits.
strings.bipe_claim_cnpj_taken: Another Bipe account already verified this CNPJ. If the company is yours, talk to Bipe Support.
strings.bipe_claim_registry_pending: Bipe has not found this CNPJ in its copy of the Receita Federal data yet. The copy changes once a month. You do not need to do anything now.
strings.bipe_claim_awaiting_proof: The CNPJ is active. Now prove that the company is yours.
strings.bipe_claim_rejected: The Receita Federal does not show this CNPJ as active.
strings.bipe_claim_registry_inactive: Not active at the Receita Federal
strings.bipe_claim_proof_title: Prove that the company is yours
strings.bipe_claim_proof_ecnpj_body: Sign the text below with the company e-CNPJ certificate, on a computer or in the certificate app. The signed file ends in .p7s. Then choose that file here.
strings.bipe_claim_signature_invalid: Bipe could not accept this signature. Check that the certificate is this company e-CNPJ and that you signed exactly the text above.
strings.bipe_claim_signature_unreadable: Bipe could not read this file. Choose the .p7s signature file.
strings.bipe_claim_verified: Business verified. The seal shows in chats and on the account profile.
strings.bipe_claim_domains_body: Show that the website belongs to the company: publish a TXT record in the website DNS and tap Verify.
strings.bipe_claim_domain_invalid: This address does not look like a website. Write only the domain, like example.com.br.
strings.bipe_claim_domain_not_yet: The record does not show yet. A DNS change can take a few hours.
strings.bipe_claim_reserved_body: The company name looks like a reserved name. The Bipe team checks before the account can use that name.
strings.bipe_claim_reserved_pending: The team still has to check
strings.bipe_claim_withdraw_confirm: Withdraw the request for this company? If the account already has the seal, it goes away.
strings.bipe_notice_safety: Bipe and institutions never ask for a password, PIN or code in a message.
strings.bipe_notice_a11y: Official notice from %1$s, an institution verified by Bipe
strings.bipe_warning_nickname_confirm_title: Is this the person you know?
strings.bipe_warning_nickname_confirm_body: You saved this contact as %1$s. The account is verified as %2$s. Is it the same person?
strings.bipe_pix_card_bank_name: Your bank will show the name %1$s. If you see another name, don't pay.
strings.bipe_pix_card_copied: Code copied. Paste it in your bank app.
strings.bipe_pix_card_status_sent: You marked it as sent. Waiting for %1$s to confirm receipt.
strings.bipe_warning_name_lookalike_emoji: This emoji can't go next to the name. It looks like a verification badge.
strings.bipe_scam_victim_body: Call your bank now and ask for a refund through MED. The sooner, the better your chance of getting the money back.
strings.bipe_settings_language_footer: Choose Portuguese or English in Bipe's settings on this phone.
strings.bipe_settings_share_presence_footer: If you turn this off, nobody sees you typing and you don't see others typing. Read receipts always stay on.
strings.bipe_about_steward: Data and servers stay in Brazil. Bipe is an experiment by Envisioning, a research institute.
strings.bipe_signup_handle_footer: People find you by your @ without seeing your number. You can choose it later.
strings.bipe_handle_too_short: Too short. Use at least %1$s characters.
strings.bipe_handle_too_long: Too long. Use at most %1$s characters.
strings.bipe_handle_invalid_characters: Use only lowercase letters, numbers, dots and underscores. Start with a letter or number and do not end with a dot.
strings.bipe_handle_taken: Someone already uses this @. Choose another.
strings.bipe_handle_screen_footer: People find you by your @ without seeing your number. After a change, wait 30 days before changing it again.
strings.bipe_handle_remove_body: Nobody can find you by @%1$s anymore, and your chats show that you no longer use it.
strings.bipe_messaging_everyone_body: People you don't know arrive as a chat request.
strings.bipe_messaging_verified_body: Accounts with a verified name can also message you. Until the badge is available, only your contacts can.
strings.bipe_messaging_contacts_body: People in a group or chat with you, people you invited and whoever invited you.
strings.bipe_error_invite_invalid: Couldn't use this invite. Ask the person who invited you for another.
strings.bipe_invite_signed_in_title_anonymous: You got an invite to Bipe
strings.bipe_invite_signed_in_body: You already have an account on this phone. Talk to this person from it, or make another account with this invite.
strings.bipe_invite_no_longer_valid: This invite is no longer valid or was already used.
strings.bipe_error_email_taken: This email is already on another Bipe account. Use a different email.
strings.bipe_error_password_weak: This password is too weak. Pick a longer or less obvious one.
strings.bipe_error_handle_cooldown: Wait 30 days between changes to your @.
strings.bipe_error_rate_limited: Too many tries. Wait a bit and try again.
strings.bipe_error_unauthorized: Get back into your account to keep using Bipe on this device.
strings.bipe_error_network: Cannot reach Bipe. Check your connection and try again.
strings.bipe_error_attestation_invalid: We couldn't confirm this is the official Bipe app. Update the app and try again.
strings.bipe_error_attestation_failed: We couldn't check this phone with Apple. Check your connection and try again.
strings.bipe_signup_display_name_footer: People see this name in chats. You can change it later.
strings.bipe_start_chat_handle_not_found: We couldn't find @%1$s on Bipe. Check the @ with the person.
strings.bipe_start_chat_search_by_handle: On Bipe, you find people by their @. Ask them for it.
strings.bipe_profile_qr_footer: Anyone who points their camera at this code opens your Bipe profile.
strings.bipe_requests_row_body: You choose who to talk to
strings.bipe_request_unverified_body: This account's name hasn't been verified yet. If you aren't sure who it is, check another way before accepting.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_pix_key: The message appears to contain a Pix key. Before paying, check the request with the person another way.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_delivery_fee: Scammers often ask for a fee by link to release a delivery. Do not pay through the link. Check the tracking in the store's app or on the Correios site.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_lookalike_link: This link appears to imitate a bank, government office or company. Check in the app or on the site you already use.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_bank_alert: The message mentions unblocking an account, card or Pix. Check the notice in your bank's app.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_pix_code: The message has a Pix copy-and-paste code. Before you pay, check with the person another way and look at the name your bank shows.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_boleto: The message has a boleto code. Fake boletos are a common scam. Before you pay, check in your bank app who gets the money.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_receipt: The message mentions a payment receipt. A screenshot of a receipt does not prove payment. Check in your bank app that the money arrived.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_new_number: The message mentions a new number or account. Call the number you already have for the person to check.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_urgency: Rush and money requests show up a lot in scams. Before you do anything, check with the person another way.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_extortion: The message makes a threat and asks for money. Paying does not usually end the threat. Do not pay, and keep the messages. SaferNet helps for free, without asking your name: new.safernet.org.br/helpline
strings.bipe_scam_warning_remote_app: The message asks you to install an app. With an app like this, someone else can use your phone from far away, and banks do not ask for that. Do not install it. Call your bank on the number on your card.
strings.bipe_scam_warning_pin_request: The message asks for a PIN or a code. Nobody from Bipe asks for your PIN, not by message and not by phone call. Do not give it to anyone.
strings.bipe_signup_invite_required: To create your account, ask someone who already uses Bipe for an invite code.
strings.bipe_invite_already_signed_in: You already have an account. Invites are for people not on Bipe yet.
strings.bipe_invites_explainer: Invite your family first. Each invite works for one person and expires in 7 days.
strings.bipe_invites_other_device: Made on another device. Share it from there.
strings.bipe_invites_share_message: Join me on Bipe. The invite only works until %2$s: %1$s
strings.bipe_invites_empty: Invite someone to chat with you on Bipe.
strings.bipe_invites_qr_footer: The other person points their phone camera at the code. After installing Bipe, they scan it again and the app opens with the invite filled in.
strings.bipe_trust_footer: Only you can see this profile.
strings.bipe_public_profile_toggle: Show my profile to people with the link
strings.bipe_public_profile_footer: People with your link see your name, photo and bio. Your profile doesn't appear in search. You can hide it whenever you want.
strings.bipe_public_profile_needs_handle: Choose a username first. Your profile link uses your @.
strings.bipe_public_profile_name_too_long: Name too long. Use at most %1$s characters.
strings.bipe_public_profile_bio_too_long: Bio too long. Use at most %1$s characters.
strings.bipe_public_profile_bio_too_many_lines: Use at most %1$s lines in the bio.
strings.bipe_public_profile_photo_invalid: That photo didn't work. Try another one.
strings.bipe_public_profile_not_verified: This profile doesn't verify the person's name
strings.bipe_public_profile_socials_footer: Type only the @handle of each account. Anyone who opens your profile sees them.
strings.bipe_public_profile_socials_not_verified: Bipe doesn't check that these accounts belong to this person
strings.bipe_public_profile_social_invalid: That handle doesn't work on %1$s. Type only the @handle, not the link.
strings.bipe_public_profile_social_reserved: That handle is reserved for verified institutions. Use your own.
strings.bipe_trust_step_email_body: Open a link we send to your email.
strings.bipe_trust_step_pix_body: A R$ 0.01 Pix from your bank account verifies your name.
strings.bipe_trust_step_govbr_body: A signature with your gov.br account verifies your name.
strings.bipe_govbr_intro: You sign a short Bipe document in the gov.br app. Then people who talk to you see your verified name.
strings.bipe_govbr_needs_level: Needs a silver or gold gov.br account.
strings.bipe_govbr_step_save: Bipe saves the document on your phone and opens the gov.br app.
strings.bipe_govbr_step_sign: In the gov.br app, tap sign document and pick bipe-verificacao.pdf.
strings.bipe_govbr_step_share: After you sign, come back to Bipe and tap Send signed document.
strings.bipe_govbr_safety: Bipe never asks for your gov.br password or code, and never sends you a document to sign in a message.
strings.bipe_govbr_guide_title: What it looks like in gov.br
strings.bipe_govbr_guide_open: In the gov.br app, sign in and tap Assinar documentos digitalmente.
strings.bipe_govbr_guide_sign: Tap the page to place your signature. Then tap Assinar.
strings.bipe_govbr_guide_authorize: The gov.br app sends you a code. Type the code and tap Autorizar.
strings.bipe_govbr_guide_save: Tap Baixar arquivo assinado and save it to Files. Then come back to Bipe and tap Send signed document.
strings.bipe_govbr_get_app: Install the gov.br app to sign.
strings.bipe_govbr_no_open_verification: To send a signed document, start with Verify with gov.br.
strings.bipe_govbr_reason_not_signed: This file has no signature. Sign it in the gov.br app and send it again.
strings.bipe_govbr_reason_not_govbr: This signature is not from gov.br.
strings.bipe_govbr_reason_wrong_document: This file is from another check. Download the document again, sign it and send it.
strings.bipe_govbr_reason_cpf_in_use: This CPF already verified another Bipe account.
strings.bipe_govbr_reason_changed_after_signing: The file changed after it was signed. Sign the original document again.
strings.bipe_trust_step_cnpj_body: We check that the CNPJ is active with the Receita Federal.
strings.bipe_trust_step_proof_body: Sign with the company's e-CNPJ, or verify your personal account as an owner or partner.
strings.bipe_trust_step_domain_body: A DNS record shows that the website belongs to the company.
strings.bipe_voice_transcribed_here: Transcribed on your phone. The audio didn't leave it.
strings.bipe_voice_transcribe_unavailable: This phone can't transcribe this language without the internet.
strings.bipe_voice_transcribe_denied: To transcribe, allow speech recognition for Bipe in the phone settings.
strings.bipe_voice_transcript_unavailable: Couldn't transcribe. You can send the audio without text.
strings.bipe_voice_kept_scam: Bipe kept this audio because of the scam warning, in case you need it for a police report.
strings.bipe_voice_keep_limit: You're already keeping %1$s audio messages. To keep this one, stop keeping another.
strings.bipe_stickers_empty_body: Save a sticker from a chat or make one from a photo.
strings.bipe_stickers_error_load: The stickers did not load. Try again.
strings.bipe_stickers_pack_share_failed: Couldn't share the pack. Try again.
strings.bipe_sticker_pack_failed: Couldn't open this pack. Try again.
strings.bipe_invite_note_footer: The message goes to your chat when they join. Until then, it stays on this phone.
strings.bipe_invite_note_default: Hi! I invited you to Bipe. Write back here.
strings.bipe_stickers_import_help: In WhatsApp, send the stickers to a group with only you in it. Then use Export chat, choose Attach media and save the file. Here, choose that file.
strings.bipe_stickers_import_help_folder_android: You can also choose the files in the WhatsApp Stickers folder.
strings.bipe_stickers_import_note: Imported stickers are stored on Bipe's server without end-to-end encryption. Only import images you can share.
strings.bipe_stickers_import_none: No new stickers in that file.
strings.bipe_stickers_import_failed: The import did not work. Try again.
strings.bipe_sticker_save_failed: Couldn't save the sticker. Try again.
strings.bipe_stickers_from_photo: Create a sticker from a photo
strings.bipe_contacts_intro: See which of your contacts are already on Bipe. The server only compares the numbers and stores none of them.
strings.bipe_contacts_denied: Bipe doesn't have access to your contacts. To allow it, open the app's settings on this phone.
strings.bipe_contacts_none: None of your contacts are on Bipe yet.
strings.bipe_contacts_invite: Invite people who are not here
strings.bipe_discovery_toggle: People who have my number can find me
strings.bipe_discovery_footer: Your number is never shown to anyone. Only people who already have you in their contacts can find you.
strings.bipe_phone_not_linked: Your number isn't linked to your account. Your contacts can't find you by it yet.
strings.bipe_phone_confirm_soon: Confirm your number by %1$s so people who have it can keep finding you.
strings.bipe_phone_confirm_expired: Confirmation expired: nobody finds you by your number.
strings.bipe_groups_empty_body: Create a group to chat with family, friends or colleagues.
strings.bipe_self_chat_error: Couldn't open your notes. Try again.
strings.bipe_onboarding_point_scam: Checks look for scam signals in messages.
strings.bipe_onboarding_point_brazil: Data and servers stay in Brazil, under Brazilian law.
strings.bipe_onboarding_point_no_ads: No ads. Your data isn't for sale.
strings.bipe_signup_device_header: Start with your name. Your @ and email are optional.
strings.bipe_signup_email_optional_footer: Helps you get back into your account if you lose your phone. It doesn't appear on your profile.
strings.bipe_signup_terms_accept: I have read and accept the %1$s and the %2$s.
strings.bipe_signup_terms_required: To create your account, accept the Terms of use and the Privacy policy.
strings.bipe_terms_reaccept_body: To keep using Bipe, read and accept the Terms of use and the Privacy policy.
strings.bipe_terms_reaccept_failed: We could not save your acceptance. Try again.
strings.bipe_pin_create_body: Choose a PIN with %1$s numbers. It locks the app and helps protect account recovery.
strings.bipe_pin_never_asked: Nobody from Bipe asks for your PIN. Not by message, not by phone call.
strings.bipe_pin_mismatch: The two PINs do not match. Try again.
strings.bipe_pin_problem_repeated_digit: Repeated digits are easy to guess. Pick another PIN.
strings.bipe_pin_problem_sequence: Sequences are easy to guess. Pick another PIN.
strings.bipe_pin_problem_date: This looks like a date, and dates are easy to guess. Pick another PIN.
strings.bipe_pin_wrong: That PIN doesn't match. Attempts left: %1$s.
strings.bipe_pin_blocked_body: The PIN locked after %1$s wrong tries. Create a new one with your recovery email.
strings.bipe_pin_change_biometric_reason: Confirm it is you to change the PIN.
strings.bipe_fallback_body: Choose a way to get back into your account if you lose your phone. Without one, you may lose access to your account.
strings.bipe_fallback_email_body: We send you a link. With the link and your PIN, the account comes back after %1$s hours.
strings.bipe_fallback_guardians_body: People you confirmed in person approve getting back into your account. Then there is a %1$s-hour wait.
strings.bipe_fallback_recovery_key_body: The key also brings back your old messages. Nobody at Bipe will ask for it.
strings.bipe_fallback_reminder: You have no way back into your account yet if you lose your phone.
strings.bipe_fallback_sync_off_ios: iCloud is off on this phone. With it on, your account comes back on a new iPhone with no wait.
strings.bipe_fallback_sync_off_android: Google backup is off on this phone. With it on, your account comes back on a new phone with no wait.
strings.bipe_pin_reminder_body: Type your %1$s-digit PIN, so you don't forget it.
strings.bipe_pin_reminder_right: That's it. See you next time.
strings.bipe_pin_reminder_wrong: That's not your PIN. If you don't remember it, change it now.
strings.bipe_email_footer: Use it to get back into your account or create a new PIN. It doesn't appear on your profile.
strings.bipe_email_sent: We sent a link to %1$s. Open it to confirm.
strings.bipe_email_link_invalid: This link no longer works. Ask for a new one in the app.
strings.bipe_email_change_reason: Confirm it's you to change the recovery email.
strings.bipe_error_email_unavailable: We cannot send email right now. Try again later.
strings.bipe_recovery_qr_body: Open Bipe on the old phone and point this phone's camera at the QR code that shows there.
strings.bipe_recovery_qr_never_from_others: Bipe never asks you to scan a QR code that someone else sent.
strings.bipe_recovery_token_found: Your account came with this phone's backup. Enter your PIN to sign in.
